September has given me the sudden urge to sort my shit out 😂

And even though we’re already half way through the month (typical me being late!) I’m starting a new series where I tackle the jobs I’ve been putting off.

You know the ones…

Because apparently I’d rather spend three weeks thinking about doing something than just bloody do it.

Basically, I’m inviting you to sort our shit out together.

And if you’re new here, my passion is to make my home as easy to maintain as possible, not perfect, and I find the cleaning hacks, tools, a bare minimum routine rather than whole house marathons and little shortcuts that actually make everyday life easier.

So follow along if you fancy it! 🥰

Save this one pan lasagne recipe 😍
cannot believe how easy it is and hardly any clean up afterwards! 🙌🏼 cosy season is coming!

Ingredients:
1 tbsp olive oil
1 onion, finely diced
2 tsp minced garlic
500g lean beef mince
750g Mutti pasta sauce
475ml chicken stock, plus extra if needed
120g ricotta cheese
Salt and pepper, to taste Italian herbs, to taste 170g lasagne sheets
120g grated mozzarella
Fresh basil and Parmesan, to serve

Method: 

Method:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large, deep frying pan over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until it starts to soften.
2. Add the garlic, season with salt and pepper and cook for another couple of minutes.
3. Turn the heat up and add the beef mince. Break it up as it cooks and fry for around 5 minutes until nicely browned.
4. Stir in the Mutti pasta sauce, chicken stock, ricotta and Italian herbs. Season again if needed and let everything simmer together for about 5 minutes.
5. Break the lasagne sheets into smaller pieces and add them straight into the pan. Use tongs to gently push the pasta down into the sauce, spreading the pieces around as evenly as you can. It does not need to be perfect.
6. Put the lid on, turn the heat right down and cook according to the instructions on your lasagne packet.
Mine took around 20 minutes. Check it occasionally to make sure nothing is sticking and add a splash more stock if the sauce starts to get too thick.

7. Once the pasta is tender, test it with a fork. It should be soft and easy to pierce.
8. Sprinkle the mozzarella over the top, cover the pan again and leave for a few minutes until the cheese has melted. If your pan is oven safe, you can instead place it under the grill for around 5 minutes until golden and bubbling.
9. Finish with fresh basil and Parmesan and serve straight from the pan.
•
Recipe adapted slightly from @noaawilliams as I didn't have any cottage cheese but will be making again with it to see the difference!
#easyrecipe #onepotmeal #easymeals #quickdinner #easydinnerideas

Solo parenting for a few days means I’ve got the whole bed to myself… so obviously I’m making it smell like a luxury hotel 😂

A few little things that make SUCH a difference:

✨ Bicarb + essential oil on the mattress to help with odours and moisture
✨ Steam clean the headboard with ironing water, makes it smell so fresh! 
✨ Fresh sheets washed in Tallow & Ash Oud - my favourite scent of theirs and it screams hotel!

You can get a bundle with all of their scents to try them and find your favourite, and it also comes with their viral stain remover pen.

Now I just need to wait until bedtime… which is proving very difficult 😂

THIS is why your dishwasher smells 🤢 
Another job we’ve been putting off… and once again, it took nowhere near as long as my brain had convinced me it would 😂

This one was requested by you guys for the procrastination series, so of course I had to time it ⏱️

Here’s what I did:

1. Removed the shelves, filter and spray arms 
2. Took apart the filter and soaked it with the spray arms in hot soapy water 
3. Cleaned the walls, base, around the door and inside the edges.
4. Cleaned the seals, although I didn’t take them off because I’ve never been brave enough 😂
5. Gave everything soaking a scrub and put it all back together.
6. Top up salt and rinse aid
7. Run a cycle with a dishwasher cleaner

And that’s it! ✨

Has anyone actually taken their dishwasher seals off? Is it easy to get them back on?!

What job should I time next? 👀
